brief: Garrett frames the AI/momentum selloff as a three-pillar story rather than a risk event, with the next move hinging on earnings confirmation (14% of SPX reports this week, 44% the week after). Pillar one: positioning is already stretched, US long/short net exposure at a 5-year low, tech saw its largest-ever one-week net selling, yet gross exposure held at 213.9%, so funds got less long but not smaller. Pillar two: breadth is improving, the market was narrow (10 names are 40% of SPX) but 350 SPX names were green last week and SPX ex-AI beat SPX by 475bps, so the selloff reads as a narrow-market unwind, not broad risk-off. Pillar three: the AI debt-burden story is not new, the alarming framing matches a year-old WSJ article, though CCC spreads and CDX IG have widened meaningfully versus VIX. Fundamental long/short managers are down 2.7% on the week and 2.8% on the month. Separately: CTAs, short bonds, are forecast to buy into Treasuries; Friday set a record for SPX put notional and the sharpest panic-index rally on record; and the AI-winners-vs-AI-at-risk pair trade, up nearly 100% through June, is now flat on the year.
